record.paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
record.original_question: Does the hierarchy of Boolean LL(k) grammar languages collapse at a finite lookahead length? More precisely, is there a number k0 > 0 such that, for every k >= k0, Boolean LL(k) grammars generate exactly the same family of languages as Boolean LL(k0) grammars? A Boolean LL(k) grammar is a Boolean grammar satisfying a uniqueness condition for generalized recursive-descent parsing with k-symbol lookahead: for each nonterminal, lookahead string of length at most k, and possible surrounding sequence of conjuncts, at most one rule can apply.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Boolean grammar is a quadruple G = (Σ, N, R, S) where Σ is a finite alphabet of terminals, N is a finite set of nonterminals, S ∈ N is the start symbol, and R is a finite set of rules of the form
    A → α₁ & … & αₘ & ¬β₁ & … & ¬βₙ ,
with m ≥ 1, n ≥ 0, and αᵢ, βⱼ ∈ (Σ ∪ N)*. The language L(G) ⊆ Σ* is defined as the least solution (or, equivalently, by any of the standard equivalent semantics) of the corresponding language equations interpreting concatenation, intersection (&), and complementation (¬) in the usual way.

For a positive integer k, a Boolean grammar G is called Boolean LL(k) if it satisfies the following uniqueness condition for generalized recursive-descent parsing with k-symbol lookahead: for every nonterminal A ∈ N, every lookahead string w ∈ Σ^{≤k}, and every admissible surrounding sequence of conjuncts that may arise during a generalized recursive-descent parse, at most one rule of A is applicable.

Let 𝓛_BLL(k) denote the family of languages generated by Boolean LL(k) grammars.

Question: Does the hierarchy {𝓛_BLL(k)}_{k ≥ 1} collapse at some finite lookahead? That is, does there exist an integer k₀ ≥ 1 such that, for every k ≥ k₀,
    𝓛_BLL(k) = 𝓛_BLL(k₀) ?
artifact.status_search_result: No source was located establishing a collapse or strict-hierarchy result for general Boolean LL(k) grammars. Related collapse results are known for restricted subclasses (e.g., LL(k)-linear conjunctive grammars can be reduced to LL(1)-linear, and the Boolean closure of linear context-free languages collapses at a finite level), but these do not address the full Boolean LL(k) hierarchy. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Transformation of LL(k)-linear to LL(1)-linear Grammars
status_evidence.snippet: Every LL(k)-linear conjunctive grammar can be transformed to an LL(1)-linear conjunctive grammar; the hierarchy with respect to k collapses.
status_evidence.claim: Collapse known for the linear-conjunctive subclass, not for general Boolean LL(k).

status_evidence.title: On LL(k) linear conjunctive grammars (Olkhovsky, Okhotin)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the LL(k) hierarchy for linear conjunctive grammars.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses only the linear conjunctive case, leaving the general Boolean LL(k) collapse question untouched.
